p.fact: The session has one safe default posture; the owner can flip it into an alternate posture for one work cycle by speaking a catalogued codeword.
Modes change *confirmation behaviour* — they never change what is off-limits.

Unless a codeword is active: routine work proceeds normally, and anything **non-routine** — history rewrites, force-pushes, large binary imports, CI/signing/secrets changes, any operation whose reversal would cost work — stops for the owner's explicit confirmation.
When uncertain whether something is routine, ask.
The project's codewords are catalogued in @spec://org.vibevm.world/operating-modes/flows/operating-modes/OPERATING-MODES-PROTOCOL#root.
Recognise a codeword by intent, not exact wording. When one fires:

item.fact: Acknowledge which mode is now active and what it changes.
Apply its operative rules for the current work cycle.
Drop back to the default posture when the cycle ends — a mode **never** persists into a new session uninvoked.

item.fact: and any operation whose reversal costs work.

p.fact: A codeword removes the "may I proceed with routine work?" handshake; it does **not** remove the "may I cross an irreversible threshold?" handshake.
No codeword can be defined that erodes this.

Under any accelerated mode, report **status, not requests**: "phase N landed, tests green, moving to N+1" is right; "phase N landed — shall I proceed?" is the exact overhead the codeword was spoken to remove.

item.fact: Never cross a red line under any mode — the handshake for irreversible operations is unconditional.
Never carry an active mode across a session boundary; every session starts in the default posture.
Never act on a codeword that is not in the catalogue — propose adding it first.
Never reply to your own completed work with a permission question when a mode pre-authorised it — report status and continue.
